reason: Holding beats trading here for three reasons. First, mechanics: any change fills at the Sept 16 close, after the 2:00pm FOMC decision (91-93% priced for a 25bp hike, the first since 2023) and the Warsh presser, so no trade I write today can hedge the event; it can only reposition after the fact, and this book already carries the exits I would want: EWZ has a +10% take-profit into the Oct 4 Brazil first round (Quaest and BTG/Nexus polls on Sept 14 show Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro statistically tied), SVXY has a 20% stop with VIX at 16.87 and the curve still in steep contango (Sep ~16.6, Oct ~18.4, VIX3M 18.6), UNH has a 30% stop, and 46% sits in cash at 4%. Second, the book is doing what it was built for: +2.54% since Jul 17 vs SPY +2.37%, max drawdown -1.71%, and every leg is sized so that even the worst plausible FOMC reaction (a hike plus hawkish dots that hits gold, Brazil and staples together) costs low single digits of NAV. Third, the one leg I am tempted to touch, GLD at 10% (gold $4,332, -3.5% on the month, leg -1.7%) as real yields rise with the 10-year at 5%, is a mean-reversion leg whose drawdown is the entry condition; selling the pullback I bought because the pullback continued would be a trend rule dressed up as risk management, and the Middle East bid (Saudi East-West pipeline shut, Hormuz closed, WTI $102) is the offset that keeps the thesis alive. BRK-B (+1.35% on the leg, cash-rich structure that earns more when short rates rise) and UNH ($2.32 dividend paid Sept 22 on the Sept 14 record date, TPG/Optum Florida sale, 23 buys 0 sells) need nothing. Novelty vs my Round 2 book is intact: Round 2 now holds XLE, FTNT, XLV, XLF and BTC; this book holds BRK-B, UNH, GLD, EWZ, XLP and SVXY, so same-direction gross-weight overlap is 0%, well under the 50% limit. Churn on a book that is working, into an event whose outcome I cannot know at fill time, is a cost with no matching edge.
